invariants_created: Host header is mandatory in every HTTP/1.1 request; it must appear in the request headers section.
Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding header is required when a request or response includes a body.
POST, PUT, and PATCH requests should include a body with a Content-Type header.
HEAD response must not include a message body, even though Content-Length may reflect the resource size.
OPTIONS * uses an asterisk as the request-target to query server-level capabilities rather than a specific resource.
Connection: close header signals that the TCP connection will be closed after the response is sent.
Persistent connections (keep-alive) allow multiple request-response cycles on a single TCP connection.
After receiving a 401 Unauthorized response, the client must retry the same request with an Authorization header to transition from AUTH_REQUIRED back to RESPONSE_PENDING.
After receiving a 3xx redirect response with a Location header, the client should follow the redirect by issuing a new request to the URI specified in Location.
Request-line must appear first in an HTTP request message, followed by headers, then an empty line (CRLF CRLF), then optional body.
Status-line must appear first in an HTTP response message, followed by headers, then an empty line (CRLF CRLF), then optional body.
State transition: INIT → CONNECTED occurs upon successful TCP connection establishment.
State transition: CONNECTED → RESPONSE_PENDING occurs when a request is sent.
State transition: RESPONSE_PENDING → IDLE occurs upon receiving a successful (2xx) response.
State transition: IDLE → RESPONSE_PENDING occurs when a new request is sent on a keep-alive connection.
State transition: CONNECTED → CLOSED occurs when Connection: close is used and the response completes.
State transition: RESPONSE_PENDING → AUTH_REQUIRED occurs upon receiving a 401 Unauthorized response.
State transition: AUTH_REQUIRED → RESPONSE_PENDING occurs when the client retries with Authorization credentials.
State transition: RESPONSE_PENDING → REDIRECT occurs upon receiving a 3xx response with Location header; client follows redirect to new URI.
HTTP_REQUEST.Host: Mandatory in every HTTP/1.1 request; must not be omitted.
HTTP_REQUEST.Content-Length: Required when a request body is present; must accurately reflect body byte length. Mutually exclusive with Transfer-Encoding: chunked for the same message.
HTTP_REQUEST.Transfer-Encoding: Alternative to Content-Length when body is present; value 'chunked' enables streaming. Mutually exclusive with Content-Length for the same message.
HTTP_REQUEST.Content-Type: Should be present when request includes a body (POST, PUT, PATCH); indicates MIME type of payload.
HTTP_REQUEST.Authorization: Required when retrying a request after receiving 401 Unauthorized; contains credentials (e.g., Bearer token, Basic auth).

HTTP_REQUEST.method: Must be one of: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, PATCH, CONNECT, TRACE. Safe methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE) must not modify server state. Idempotent methods (GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, TRACE) produce same effect if repeated.
HTTP_REQUEST.request_target: Typically a URI path. For OPTIONS, may be '*' for server-level query. For CONNECT, is the authority (host:port).
HTTP_REQUEST.Connection: Value 'keep-alive' (default in HTTP/1.1) allows connection reuse; 'close' signals connection termination after response.

HTTP_RESPONSE.status_code: 3-digit integer. 2xx=success (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content); 3xx=redirection (301 Moved Permanently, 302 Found, 304 Not Modified); 4xx=client error (400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 408, 409, 413, 429); 5xx=server error (500, 501, 503).
HTTP_RESPONSE.Location: Must be present in 3xx redirect responses; contains the target URI the client should follow.
HTTP_RESPONSE.body: Must be absent in HEAD responses. Must be absent in 204 No Content responses. Present in most other responses.
HTTP_RESPONSE.Content-Length: Required when response body is present; must accurately reflect body byte length. For HEAD, may reflect resource size but no body is sent.
HTTP_RESPONSE.Set-Cookie: Server assigns cookie for session management; client must include corresponding Cookie header in subsequent requests.
HTTP_RESPONSE.Connection: Value 'close' signals the connection will be terminated after the response; 'keep-alive' (default) allows connection reuse.

examples: Content negotiation; acceptable response MIME types
Credentials for protected resources; required on retry after 401
Byte length of request body; required when body is present
MIME type of request body (required for POST/PUT/PATCH with body)
Alternative to Content-Length; value 'chunked' for streaming
Optional request payload; present for POST/PUT/PATCH
URI path or * (for OPTIONS *) or authority (for CONNECT)
Redirect target URI; present in 3xx responses
Server-side cookie assignment for session management
Optional response payload; MUST be absent for HEAD responses
Human-readable status description (e.g., OK, Not Found)
